reference.source: Bradley and Daroff's Neurology in Clinical Practice
clinicalPearls: Subacute onset (days to weeks) of short-term memory impairment, temporal lobe seizures, confusion and neuropsychiatric change (anxiety, depression, hallucinations, personality change) is the core syndrome.
Anterograde amnesia with relative preservation of remote memory reflects selective hippocampal and medial temporal involvement.
Small-cell lung carcinoma with anti-Hu (ANNA-1) is the commonest association; anti-Ma2 disease characteristically affects young men with testicular germ-cell tumours.
Cell-surface antibody syndromes (anti-NMDAR, anti-LGI1, anti-GABA-B, anti-AMPAR, anti-CASPR2) are considerably more responsive to immunotherapy than intracellular onconeural antibody syndromes.
Anti-LGI1 disease produces faciobrachial dystonic seizures and hyponatraemia and is often non-paraneoplastic, though thymoma may occur.
Anti-GABA-B encephalitis presents with prominent early seizures and is strongly linked to small-cell lung carcinoma.
MRI typically shows unilateral or bilateral medial temporal T2/FLAIR hyperintensity, and CSF shows lymphocytic pleocytosis, raised protein and oligoclonal bands.
The syndrome frequently antedates the tumour diagnosis by months, so a negative initial cancer screen warrants periodic re-screening.
reference.pathophysiology: An immune response directed against a tumour that ectopically expresses neuronal antigens cross-reacts with limbic structures (hippocampi, amygdala, cingulate and insular cortex), producing inflammation and neuronal loss. Two mechanistic groups exist: antibodies against intracellular onconeural antigens (Hu/ANNA-1, Ma2, CV2/CRMP5, amphiphysin) are markers of a predominantly cytotoxic T-cell mediated process that is poorly reversible, whereas antibodies against neuronal cell-surface or synaptic proteins (NMDAR, LGI1, GABA-B, AMPAR, CASPR2) are directly pathogenic, disrupt receptor function or clustering, and are potentially reversible with immunotherapy.
additionalDifferentials: herpes simplex and other viral encephalitides
primary CNS lymphoma or gliomatosis cerebri
additionalInvestigations: paired serum and CSF autoimmune and paraneoplastic antibody panel
MRI brain with contrast (medial temporal FLAIR sequences)
CSF analysis with oligoclonal bands and cytology
whole-body FDG-PET/CT to detect occult malignancy
CT chest for small-cell lung carcinoma or thymoma
redFlags: rapidly progressive decline in consciousness or coma
identification of an underlying malignancy requiring urgent staging
reference.prognosis: Cell-surface antibody syndromes often improve substantially with tumour treatment and immunotherapy, whereas intracellular onconeural antibody-associated disease tends to leave persistent cognitive deficits. Overall outcome is governed by the antibody type and the stage and treatability of the underlying tumour.
pitfalls: Misdiagnosing as herpes simplex encephalitis and missing the paraneoplastic search.
Assuming a negative antibody panel excludes the diagnosis, since seronegative cases are recognised.
Abandoning the tumour hunt after one negative screen rather than repeating surveillance.
Overlooking an occult testicular germ-cell tumour in a young man with anti-Ma2 antibodies.
references: Graus F, et al. A clinical approach to diagnosis of autoimmune encephalitis. Lancet Neurology.
Dalmau J, Rosenfeld MR. Paraneoplastic and autoimmune encephalitis.
Bradley and Daroff's Neurology in Clinical Practice, current edition.
management: Identification and treatment of the underlying tumour where present, alongside immunotherapy

First-line immunotherapy with corticosteroids, intravenous immunoglobulin or plasma exchange, escalating to rituximab or cyclophosphamide, with better response in cell-surface antibody syndromes than onconeural ones
Seizure control with anticonvulsants, including targeting faciobrachial dystonic seizures in anti-LGI1 disease
Correction of hyponatraemia and neuropsychiatric supportive care
Systematic malignancy search, including testicular ultrasound in young men with anti-Ma2, and repeated surveillance if initially negative
Coordinated neurology and oncology multidisciplinary management with cognitive rehabilitation
